beats.text: She went to space, then onto Star Trek.

overlays.hook: She went to space, *then onto Star Trek.*

beats.text: Growing up in Chicago, she watched Star Trek, and Lieutenant Uhura, played by Nichelle Nichols.
At sixteen, she went to Stanford. Then she became a medical doctor.
She served as a Peace Corps doctor in Sierra Leone and Liberia.
In 1987, NASA picked her, one of fifteen chosen from about two thousand applicants.
On September 12, 1992, the shuttle Endeavour lifted off.
She became the first African American woman in space.
And she opened her shifts with Uhura's own line: hailing frequencies open.
She also carried a photo of the aviator Bessie Coleman.

visual.caption: Mae Jemison at work in Spacelab, 1992

beats.text: For eight days she ran experiments, on bone cells, frog eggs and motion sickness.

visual.caption: Testing motion sickness training in orbit

beats.text: That same year, she appeared on Star Trek: The Next Generation. The first real astronaut on Star Trek.
Star Trek showed her space. She went, and came back a real astronaut.

facts.claim: Raised in Chicago; Star Trek and Nichols as Uhura inspired her.
Left for Stanford at 16 (1973); MD Cornell 1981.
Peace Corps medical officer, Sierra Leone and Liberia, 1983-85.
Selected 1987, one of 15 from about 2,000 applicants.
First African American woman in space.
Carried a photo of Bessie Coleman.
About 8 days (12-20 Sept); bone cell, frog, motion sickness experiments.
Appeared in TNG "Second Chances" (1993); first real astronaut on Star Trek.
